hints: Express the given condition as a probability statement: $\mathrm{P}(T > 0.9) = 0.95$, which means the lower tail is $\mathrm{P}(T < 0.9) = 0.05$.
Use standard normal tables to find the critical $z$-value corresponding to a lower-tail area of $0.05$: $z = -1.645$.
Set up the standardisation equation $\dfrac{0.9 - m}{0.35} = -1.645$ and solve for $m$.
walkthrough:
We are given that 95% of times exceed 0.9 hours. This means the probability of taking less than 0.9 hours is $1 - 0.95 = 0.05$:
$$\mathrm{P}(T < 0.9) = 0.05$$

Start with the standardization formula that turns any normal value $T$ into a standard Z-score:
$$Z = \frac{T - m}{\sigma}$$

Look up the cumulative area of $0.05$ in the standard normal tables. Because $0.05$ is in the bottom tail below the average, the Z-score is negative:
$$\Phi(-z) = 0.05 \implies z = -1.645$$

Substitute $Z = -1.645$, $T = 0.9$, and $\sigma = 0.35$ into the standardization formula:
$$-1.645 = \frac{0.9 - m}{0.35}$$

Multiply both sides by the denominator $0.35$ to clear the fraction:
$$-1.645 \times 0.35 = 0.9 - m$$
$$-0.57575 = 0.9 - m$$

Add $m$ to both sides and add $0.57575$ to both sides to solve for the mean $m$:
$$m = 0.9 + 0.57575 = 1.47575 \approx 1.48\text{ hours}$$

hints: Find the probability that a single car takes at most 2 hours: $\mathrm{P}(T < 2)$.
Standardise $T = 2$ using your mean $m \approx 1.476$ from part (i) and standard deviation $\sigma = 0.35$: $z = \dfrac{2 - 1.476}{0.35}$.
Look up $\Phi(z)$ in the normal distribution table to evaluate $\mathrm{P}(T < 2)$.
Because the 4 cars are fitted independently, raise the single-car probability to the 4th power: $[\mathrm{P}(T < 2)]^4$.
walkthrough:
For a single car, calculate its standardized Z-score at $T = 2\text{ hours}$ using the mean $m = 1.47575$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 0.35$:
$$Z = \frac{T - m}{\sigma} = \frac{2 - 1.47575}{0.35}$$

Perform the subtraction in the numerator and then divide:
$$Z = \frac{0.52425}{0.35} = 1.49786 \approx 1.50$$

Look up $Z = 1.50$ in the cumulative normal distribution table to find the probability that one car takes at most 2 hours:
$$\mathrm{P}(T < 2) = \Phi(1.50) = 0.9332$$

Because the 4 cars are fitted independently, apply the multiplication rule. Multiply the probability 4 times (raise to the fourth power):
$$\text{Probability} = (0.9332)^4 = 0.9332 \times 0.9332 \times 0.9332 \times 0.9332 \approx 0.758$$

hints: Express the standard deviation in terms of the mean using the given relation: $\mu = 3\sigma \implies \sigma = \dfrac{\mu}{3}$.
Set up the standardisation expression for $T > 0.6\mu$: $z = \dfrac{0.6\mu - \mu}{\sigma}$.
Substitute $\sigma = \dfrac{\mu}{3}$ and cancel $\mu$ to find the numerical $z$-score.
Use normal symmetry: $\mathrm{P}(Z > -1.2) = \Phi(1.2)$, then look up $\Phi(1.2)$ in the normal table.
walkthrough:
We are given that $\mu = 3\sigma$ and want to find $\mathrm{P}(T < 0.6\mu)$. Start by setting up the standardization equation:
$$Z = \frac{T - \mu}{\sigma} = \frac{0.6\mu - \mu}{\sigma}$$

Subtract the terms in the numerator ($0.6\mu - 1.0\mu = -0.4\mu$):
$$Z = \frac{-0.4\mu}{\sigma}$$

Substitute the relationship $\mu = 3\sigma$ into the numerator:
$$Z = \frac{-0.4(3\sigma)}{\sigma} = \frac{-1.2\sigma}{\sigma}$$

Cancel the common factor $\sigma$ from both numerator and denominator:
$$Z = -1.2$$

Because the Z-score is negative, use the symmetry property of the normal distribution curve $\Phi(-z) = 1 - \Phi(z)$:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z < -1.2) = 1 - \Phi(1.2)$$

Look up $\Phi(1.2)$ in the normal distribution table ($0.8849$) and subtract from 1:
$$\mathrm{P}(T < 0.6\mu) = 1 - 0.8849 = 0.1151 \approx 0.115$$
